subject: GovCloud pilot: DPA pathing, UK Addendum & transfer safeguards
messages:
From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@govcloud.co.uk>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:03+00:00
Subject: GovCloud pilot: DPA scoping & UK IDTA implications

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking time to scope the GovCloud pilot — we need to align on DPA amendments and international transfer safeguards before procurement can progress. A few asks from our side to get to Procurement/Legal sign-off: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the UK Addendum (UK IDTA) as an alternative transfer mechanism for the pilot (we may require it in addition to SCCs)?
- Please provide a current subprocessors list with processing locations and a short note on whether any subprocessor processes Controller data outside the UK/EU for this project.
- For higher-risk telemetry (debug logs, stack traces), Procurement asks whether telemetry can be routed to GovCloud-only endpoints or kept onshore for EU/UK users.

I've attached a short procurement checklist and the procurement team's standard ask. If you can push a redlined DPA and an SCCs->UK Addendum mapping sheet that calls out where we would still need contractual language, that would help accelerate the DocuSign flow.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync Wednesday 10–10:30 BST?

Best,
Sara Miller
Head of Compliance
GovCloud Services Ltd.

Attachments: procurement_checklist.pdf (stated), initial_requirements.xlsx (stated)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Miller <sara.miller@govcloud.co.uk>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:07:12+00:00
Subject: Re: GovCloud pilot: DPA scoping & UK IDTA implications

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Sending an initial package here to make Procurement's life easier. Summary below and attachments included.

Quick answers up front: 
- Redwood can sign a UK Addendum (we accept UK IDTA style language) for the pilot, provided the pilot scope is limited to the GovCloud tenant and we keep the same subprocessors commitments in the DPA. We will highlight the clauses that need to be tightened for the full production rollout.
- Subprocessor list attached (S3). We have two potential subprocessors that operate outside EU/UK for certain infra (CDN analytics and third-party model telemetry). Both can be scoped out or have contractual constraints for the pilot; see the notes in the spreadsheet.
- Telemetry: we can implement routing controls to send debug telemetry only to GovCloud endpoints for EU/UK principals. That will be a configuration option on Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted accounts we can offer a routing policy and limited sampling.

Attachments included: DPA_draft_GovCloud_v1.pdf, SCCs-to-UK-IDTA-mapping.xlsx, subprocessor_inventory.csv

Action items I propose: 
1) Internal: Jonas to confirm technical feasibility and any latency/feature tradeoffs for telemetry routing by 2026-08-31 EOD.
2) Internal: Laura to prepare redline of the DPA showing UK Addendum acceptance language + any carve-outs.
3) External/Joint: Set a DocuSign route for the UK Addendum once Procurement confirms the final subprocessor stance.

I can take the Wed 10–10:30 BST slot. 

—
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

(Attachment stubs: DPA_draft_GovCloud_v1.pdf, SCCs-to-UK-IDTA-mapping.xlsx, subprocessor_inventory.csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Miller <sara.miller@govcloud.co.uk>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:42:55+00:00
Subject: Re: GovCloud pilot: DPA scoping & UK IDTA implications

Kimberly / Sara — adding a few technical clarifications to help Legal/Procurement decide on narrow vs broad commitments. Quoting the relevant ask: 

> "For higher-risk telemetry (debug logs, stack traces), Procurement asks whether telemetry can be routed to GovCloud-only endpoints or kept onshore for EU/UK users."

- For Dedicated and Private deployments (what GovCloud pilot will use), we have a routing policy scope that binds model-serving telemetry and user-level request metadata to a tenant-local ingestion endpoint. That means telemetry can be kept within the GovCloud VPC/region.
- For Hosted accounts (multi-tenant) we can't guarantee full tenancy separation for telemetry without dedicated capacity; however we can implement a sampling filter and mask PII fields prior to emission.
- Subprocessors: the CDN analytics subprocessor collects aggregated metrics in non-identifiable form; it can be disabled for pilot tenants. The model telemetry vendor (calls it "inference-ops") supports EU-only processing upon request but requires a short subprocessor addendum (we already have a template).

Technical risk notes: disabling CDN analytics may reduce frontend error visibility; disabling model telemetry disables some production alerting. If Procurement needs a hard onshore-only guarantee for all telemetry for the pilot, our recommended approach is: Dedicated GovCloud tenant + addendum to subprocessors + configuration toggle to route telemetry to GovCloud endpoints. That's feasible within 2–3 weeks of sign-off.

If useful, I can add a one-page tech appendix for the DPA redline that maps every telemetry class to an onshore/offshore option.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
